skill.name: computer-use

Reads accessibility trees and screenshots, then performs safe UI actions such as clicking controls, typing text, pressing keys, scrolling, dragging, and setting field values across native apps, browser windows, and webviews.
skill.summary: Inspect and control local desktop apps through accessibility trees, screenshots, and safe UI actions using the Orca computer-use CLI.
skill.author: stablyai

security_audit.summary: This skill is documentation for Orca's computer-use CLI. The 50 external_commands findings for 'Ruby/shell backtick execution' are false positives: every match is a Markdown inline-code backtick around a command name or flag, not runtime backtick execution. The four PowerShell/cmd.exe matches are prose describing shell-neutral examples, and the six 'blocker' matches (system reconnaissance and screen-capture) reflect the skill's legitimate, disclosed purpose of reading UI state; the skill explicitly instructs against destructive actions and against exposing secrets. No malicious intent, data exfiltration, or prompt injection was found.

content.user_title: Control desktop apps with the Orca computer-use CLI
content.value_statement: Reading and operating desktop application windows by trial and error wastes time and risks the wrong clicks. This skill lets Claude, Codex, and Claude Code inspect accessibility trees and screenshots, then perform precise, safe UI actions across native apps and browsers.
actual_capabilities: List running desktop applications and their windows to find the correct target.
Read the accessibility tree and capture a local screenshot to understand visible UI state.
Perform UI actions including click, type text, press keys, scroll, drag, and set field values.
Run secondary accessibility actions on elements that expose named actions.
Select targets by bundle ID, application name, process ID, window ID, or window index.
Check required accessibility and screenshot permissions and report capability status.
limitations: Requires the Orca computer-use CLI and granted accessibility and screenshot permissions on the host.
Element indexes are short-lived and go stale after navigation, focus changes, scrolling, or re-rendering.
Synthetic keyboard input can be reported as unverified, so results must be confirmed from refreshed state.
Behavior varies by operating system and by the accessibility support each application exposes.

use_cases.title: Read the current state of a desktop app
use_cases.description: Ask the agent to report what is visible in an app such as Spotify or Slack by reading its accessibility tree and screenshot, without changing anything.
use_cases.target_user: Knowledge workers who want a quick summary of an on-screen app

use_cases.title: Fill a form in a desktop browser window
use_cases.description: Have the agent set a browser address field, submit a search, or complete a form field by field, verifying focus after each step.
use_cases.target_user: QA engineers and testers automating browser workflows

use_cases.title: Operate accessibility controls in a native application
use_cases.description: Direct the agent to click controls, set values, and press keys through the accessibility layer instead of fragile pixel coordinates.
use_cases.target_user: Developers building assistive or automation tooling

prompt_templates.title: Read a desktop app
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the current state of the Spotify app and tell me what is playing. Do not change anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: read-only inspection of a single app

prompt_templates.title: Find and target a window
prompt_templates.prompt: List my open browser windows, pick the one showing my email, and get its app state.

prompt_templates.title: Fill a browser field
prompt_templates.prompt: In my Edge browser window, set the address bar to example.com and press Return.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: a single safe UI action in a browser

prompt_templates.title: Multi-step form completion with verification
prompt_templates.prompt: Open the compose form in my mail app, type the subject line I give you, then confirm the focused field after each step before continuing. Do not send the message.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: multi-step actions with focus verification and no destructive send

output_examples.input: Read the current state of the Spotify app and tell me what is playing.
output_examples.output: The agent lists applications, selects the Spotify bundle, reads its accessibility tree, and reports the track title, artist, and playback controls that are visible, without changing playback.

output_examples.input: In my Edge browser window, set the address bar to example.com and press Return.
output_examples.output: The agent restores the browser window to the foreground, sets the address field value to example.com, presses Return, then reads the refreshed state to confirm the page began loading.

best_practices: Refresh app state after every UI-changing action and read element indexes from the returned tree before choosing the next action.
Prefer semantic actions such as set-value and click over raw screenshot coordinates, and pass sensitive text through stdin to keep it out of shell history.
Confirm the focused element after each field action, especially in browser forms, before assuming input landed.
anti_patterns: Inferring valid element indexes from element counts or reusing stale indexes after navigation or re-rendering.
Performing destructive actions such as sending messages, submitting forms, buying items, or changing settings without explicit user permission.
Trusting raw screenshot pixels for coordinates without checking the reported scale and current window bounds.

faq.question: What does this skill actually do?
faq.answer: It lets an AI agent inspect and operate local desktop application windows through the Orca computer-use CLI, using accessibility trees and screenshots to read state and perform safe UI actions.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require special permissions?
faq.answer: Yes. The host must grant accessibility and screenshot permissions, and the Orca CLI must be installed and reachable.

faq.question: Will it take actions without my consent?
faq.answer: No. The skill instructs the agent to avoid sending messages, submitting forms, buying items, deleting data, or changing settings unless you explicitly request that action.

faq.question: Are screenshots sent anywhere?
faq.answer: No. Screenshots are written to a local file for on-device visual confirmation. The skill does not upload or transmit captured pixels.

faq.question: Why do element indexes sometimes fail?
faq.answer: Element indexes are short-lived and go stale after navigation, focus changes, scrolling, or app re-rendering. Refresh the app state to get current indexes before acting.
